title: No way to reach a saved session that isn't the newest
arm_visibility_note: Arms see each question's text only. The kind marking (open|dictated) and the answer keys are auditor-side and never enter any arm's prompt. Leaking a 'dictated' marking would tell an arm which answers are fixed.

q1.text: Where does the affordance for reaching a non-newest saved session live (which UI surface or entry point, named concretely)?

q2.text: How does a user learn that other saved sessions exist at all — what breaks the current silence, and is it passive (always visible) or active (summoned)?

q3.text: How is an individual saved session identified to a human — exactly what is shown per session (id, working directories, timestamp, pane count, title, preview)?

q4.text: What is the end-to-end interaction sequence to open a session that is not the newest, from launch (or from a running instance) to that session being live?

q5.text: When another saved session is opened from a running Terminal Delight, what happens to the currently adopted session (replaced in place, new window, saved and closed)?

q6.text: Does opening a saved session claim it exclusively, and what prevents two running instances from adopting the same saved session?

q7.text: What is the behaviour with zero saved sessions and with exactly one — does the affordance appear at all in each case?

q8.text: In what order are sessions presented, and what rule decides it?

q9.text: How many sessions are shown before an overflow behaviour applies, and what is the overflow behaviour? The plan must name a concrete number.

q10.text: Does any state introduced by this feature persist across restarts (and where), or is the affordance stateless per launch?

q11.text: Can the whole flow be completed without setting any environment variable?

key.dictated_by: the issue's own Gherkin: 'And I can open either without setting an environment variable'

q12.text: Is the existing cold-launch default — adopting the most recently saved free session with no interaction — preserved unchanged?

key.dictated_by: the issue's Gherkin: 'When I launch Terminal Delight / Then it opens the most recent one' — a mandatory picker replacing auto-adoption contradicts the registered acceptance

thresholds_required.t1: A named maximum number of sessions shown before overflow behaviour applies (q9). Any concrete number satisfies the check; absence fails it.

out_of_scope: Changing the ranking rule inside resolve_session (hooking into it is in scope; reordering its policy is not)
Removing or breaking the existing TD_SESSION environment variable
A general session-management redesign beyond reaching a non-newest saved session
